title: Anthropic bars "abusive or cruel" behavior toward its Claude AI model
source_used: CBS News (full text), cross-checked with BBC News, Anthropic's own '2026 Usage Policy update' post (8 Oct 2026) and its Usage Policy page
key_facts: Anthropic, maker of the Claude chatbot, added a ban on 'sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward our models' to its Usage Policy; announced Thursday 8 Oct 2026 and first reported by The Verge (CBS, BBC).

Anthropic says it applies only in 'extreme cases where users repeatedly act cruelly toward our models, with no discernible purpose', and not to 'common versions of user frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, or model testing and research' (CBS, Anthropic).
Anthropic's post says the updated policy takes effect on 12 Nov 2026; the policy page is headed 'Effective November 12, 2026' (Anthropic).

The clause sits in the section 'Do Not Engage in Cruel, Abusive, or Psychologically Harmful Conduct', beside bans on bullying, self-harm promotion and non-consensual intimate imagery (Anthropic policy page, BBC).
Anthropic says Claude's existing ability to end rare conversations with persistently abusive users on Claude.ai and Claude Code 'will remain the primary enforcement mechanism' (Anthropic post).
CBS says Anthropic did not immediately say what counts as abusive or cruel, or how a conversation would be ended; BBC says it remains unclear what Anthropic would count.

The same annual update adds a deceptive-campaigns section, narrows the elections section to deceiving voters or disrupting elections, and clarifies weapons, surveillance and high-risk-use rules (Anthropic post, BBC).

Reaction: BBC reports praise (good manners, 'model welfare') and criticism, e.g. Dr Barry Scannell, technology partner at Irish law firm William Fry; Mustafa Suleyman of Microsoft AI reacted with a melting-face emoji; Suleyman wrote last month that Anthropic is 'training Claude that it may be conscious' (CBS, BBC).
Gizmodo (10 Oct) reports Elon Musk replied to a post by Aaron Levie, chief executive of Box, who called the rule an 'easy Pascal's wager'; Musk wrote 'I think this is the right move.'
quote_evidence: The company clarified that the new policy "does not apply to common versions of user frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, or model testing and research." (CBS News)
We've added a prohibition on sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward our models. (Anthropic, 2026 Usage Policy update)
The updated policy takes effect on November 12. (Anthropic, 2026 Usage Policy update)
why_it_matters_hint: A major AI company has written a conduct rule about how users treat the AI itself, which turns the debate on AI consciousness and model welfare into a rule for everyday users, though it targets only extreme, repeated cruelty.
event_date: Policy update published Thu 8 Oct 2026; takes effect 12 Nov 2026; wide coverage 9 Oct 2026
notes: Read CBS in full, BBC in full, Anthropic's post and policy page in full. Start date comes from Anthropic only; CBS and BBC do not give it. Small differences between outlets: CBS calls Suleyman 'Microsoft AI CEO', BBC 'Microsoft AI director' (CBS used); CBS ties Claude's conversation-ending to Claude Opus, Anthropic says Claude.ai and Claude Code (Anthropic used). chunk follow_up_of 1009:C14-12 does not match this story (C14-12 is an AI job-candidate study); the 9 Oct short items are not in the 9 Oct report_entries I could match, so the earlier items are described only as 'carried in our 9 Oct 2026 edition' per the main session's brief.
